reader_reconstruction.Problem: A Gaussian RBF classifier can predict a different class from its nearest labeled prototype because it combines responses through coefficients learned from the complete labeled sample.
reader_reconstruction.Why the region matters: The nearest-prototype summary requires an explicit scope across changing bandwidth and penalty. Pointwise agreement does not establish that scope.
reader_reconstruction.Existing knowledge: Prior work supplies finite-scale equivalence for exponential potentials, mechanisms for coefficient-induced prototype mismatch, coefficient-regularized RBF statistical theory, and guarantees along fixed-design regularization paths.
reader_reconstruction.Research question: For a fixed query, training sample, and selected labeled prototypes, which computable conditions certify or exclude equality with the nearest-prototype label as Gaussian width and ridge penalty vary together?
reader_reconstruction.Approach: Bound the learned-readout residual against prototype-class reference weights across full-width families. Use limiting votes for finite disagreement thresholds and signed finite-penalty correction bounds over local width bands.
reader_reconstruction.Findings: At K=100, t=s_C, and zero penalty floor, original combined tests exclude 88.10% of MNIST and 84.48% of Fashion-MNIST queries. All 328 archived 95%-competitive readouts have zero full-width sufficient coverage. Local bands add guarantees; finite sampled paths include returns to agreement.
reader_reconstruction.Contribution: A training-derived continuous analysis of nearest-prototype label persistence with sufficient agreement, strict disagreement within a requested family, and unresolved outputs, plus an empirical account of their reach.
